newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks sprint home to record close.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks sprint home to record close.

text.p: Australian shares sprinted home to a record close on Wednesday as an afternoon rally pushed an already Dow-inspired market to higher territory.
A positive profit result from ANZ Bank and a surge in bellwether BHP after settlement of a tax dispute lit the fuse, pushing the key sharemarket barometer further ahead.

The All Ordinaries index rose 26.7 points to 2,392.7 after reaching an intraday high of 2394.7, just 3.9 points off its record high. "The banks and the top miners are the ones that have pulled the market along today," said Jim Tredenick, senior dealer at brokerage Nevitts Ltd.
"The result from ANZ Bank was good and that has fuelled the banks along," he said, citing strong performances from Westpac and National Australia Bank as well as ANZ.
ANZ reported a 6.7 percent rise in annual net profit to A$1.12 billion (US$900 million).

In the resources sector, BHP was the star in a day of strong performances. BHP shares surging to close over three percent higher after it announced it had settled a resource rent tax dispute with the state of Victoria.
The company said the dispute settlement would see a A$167 million benefit to its bottom line.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about eight to five, while about 39 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
